title: Anthony of Padua (13 June)
hook: a great Franciscan preacher, now asked to find lost things

segments.voice: Yesterday, Barnabas, who walked Saul into a room that feared him. Your line was son of encouragement.

Keys. Glasses. A ring. A passport the night before a flight. Somewhere, right now, someone is turning a couch cushion over again and saying, half joking and half not, Saint Anthony, help. Day one thousand on this path, and its saint is one whose name gets said in kitchens and parking lots. But he started as a voice that filled a square. Today, Anthony of Padua.
screen: `KEYS. GLASSES. A RING.` → `SAINT ANTHONY, HELP.` → `A VOICE THAT FILLED A SQUARE.`

segments.voice: Anthony was born in Lisbon, in Portugal, and became a canon, then a Franciscan friar, drawn to the order of Francis of Assisi while Francis was still alive. He hoped to go to Morocco as a missionary. Illness sent him back, a storm blew his ship off course, and he ended up in Italy, an unknown friar. Then one day, the story goes, at an ordination no one was ready to preach, and Anthony was told to say something. He opened his mouth, and the room discovered he knew the Scriptures deeply. From then on he preached across Italy and France, to crowds that filled churches and spilled into squares. The Church later named him a Doctor of the Church. So how does a great preacher become the saint of lost keys? Tradition says a young friar who was leaving the order took Anthony's book of psalms with him, a book Anthony had filled with notes for his preaching. Anthony prayed for it. The young man returned the book, and came back to the community too. Something precious lost and found, and a person along with it. That's an old pattern in the Gospels. Jesus tells of a woman who sweeps her whole house for one silver coin, and when she finds it she calls in the neighbors. In the Douay-Rheims: "Rejoice with me, because I have found the groat which I had lost." In Catholic teaching, asking Anthony's help isn't a lucky charm. It's asking a friend in heaven to pray with you, as you'd ask a friend at the table. And some pray to him for things bigger than keys: a lost faith, a lost child, a friendship gone quiet.
screen: `FROM LISBON TO AN UNKNOWN FRIAR.` · `THE PREACHER NO ONE EXPECTED.` · `THE BOOK OF PSALMS, RETURNED.` · `A FRIEND ASKED TO PRAY WITH YOU.` · then, large: `I HAVE FOUND THE GROAT WHICH I HAD LOST.`

segments.voice: Let one lost thing come to mind, small and annoying, or not a thing at all: a habit of prayer, a person you've drifted from. Name it plainly, once, and don't search yet; just hold it, the way the woman lit her candle before she swept. If you pray, ask Saint Anthony to pray with you for it; if you don't, simply admit you'd like it back.
Padua, the Italian city linked to the Franciscan preacher Anthony, born in Lisbon, now asked by Catholics to help them find what's lost.
Your line: finder of lost things. In his story, a book came home, and a person came with it. One thousand days now.

howItsDone: The Church keeps the memorial of Saint Anthony of Padua on 13 June; Catholics ask his intercession when something is lost, and some parishes bless and hand out bread on his feast, called Saint Anthony's bread, for the poor.

chat.says: Why do people ask Saint Anthony to help them find their keys?
options: Tradition says his lost book of psalms came back after he prayed; people ask him to pray with them.
Because he worked as a locksmith in Lisbon before joining the friars, so keys were his trade.
Because he once found Saint Francis's lost body after it was hidden under the church in Assisi.
chat.meaning: A friar took Anthony's book of psalms; Anthony prayed, and it came back. Catholics ask his help as a friend in heaven who prays with them, not a charm.
